questions.modelAnswer: To investigate how the extension of a spring, and of a rubber band, varies with the applied force.

questions.stem: Name two safety precautions for the spring and rubber-band practical.
questions.modelAnswer: Wear goggles in case the spring or band snaps, and secure the clamp stand with a G-clamp so it cannot topple.

questions.stem: Explain why the extension, not the total length, is plotted against the applied force.
questions.modelAnswer: The original length already exists at zero force; only the extra stretch answers to the load. Plotting extension isolates the stretch the force causes, so the graph reveals the material's own behaviour rather than its fixed size.

questions.stem: A spring's original length is 12.0 cm; with five masses attached its average length is 15.2 cm. Calculate the extension.
The metal wire's extension is read from:

options.explanation: No colour mechanism exists here.

options.text: The tape marker's movement past the reference point
options.explanation: New marker reading minus reference reading — the wire's rule of record.
The hanger holds loads; it is not the reading device.
Unmeasured and irrelevant to the reading.

questions.stem: The force applied by each load is calculated as:

options.explanation: No length enters the force law.
The relationship multiplies by g.
Extension is the other axis entirely.

options.text: mass × g, i.e. 0.1 kg × 10 N/kg per 100 g mass
options.explanation: The load's weight — the force of record.

questions.stem: How is the extension of the spring or rubber band calculated?

options.explanation: The subtraction of record for the spring and band.
That reverses the subtraction and returns a negative.
Multiplying lengths is meaningless here.
The original length must be removed.

questions.stem: A straight-line force-extension graph indicates that:

options.explanation: A snapped sample gives no usable line.

options.text: The force was applied too slowly
options.explanation: Application speed is not what the line shows.

options.text: The force is proportional to the extension
options.explanation: Linearity is the proportionality verdict.
The line is about the material, not the counting.

questions.stem: Parallax error in the ruler readings is avoided by:

options.text: Reading the ruler at eye level
options.explanation: Eye-level alignment removes the reading-angle bias of record.
Length of the ruler is irrelevant.
Darkness worsens readings.
Guessing is the error, not the cure.

questions.stem: State how the force applied by each 100 g load is calculated.
questions.modelAnswer: Multiply the mass by g: 0.1 kg × 10 N/kg = 1.0 N per load.

questions.stem: State the wire's extension reading rule.
questions.modelAnswer: Subtract the reference-point reading from the new tape-marker reading.

questions.stem: Explain why each reading is taken only after the load has fully settled.
questions.modelAnswer: The spring or wire keeps stretching briefly after the load lands. Reading too early records a length that is still changing — a random error — so the of-record discipline waits for the full extension before reading.
